study type: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of a national database
cohort: The study included 113,445 very low birth weight (VLBW) infants, defined as preterm infants with a birth weight less than 1500g, from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) datasets.
finding: Placental abruption is significantly associated with an increased prevalence of both intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) and severe IVH in very low birth weight infants.
